name: Cisco ASA — Outbound C2 Connection Allowed (Post DNS Resolve)
xql_query:
dataset = cisco_asa_raw
| filter _raw_log contains "302013"
| alter src_host = _json -> generalCiscoLog.src_ip,
        dst_host = _json -> generalCiscoLog.dst_ip,
        src_port = to_integer(_json -> generalCiscoLog.src_port),
        dst_port = to_integer(_json -> generalCiscoLog.dst_port),
        src_if   = _json -> generalCiscoLog.src_interface,
        dst_if   = _json -> generalCiscoLog.dst_interface,
        proto    = _json -> generalCiscoLog.protocol,
        bytes_n  = to_integer(_json -> generalCiscoLog.transferred_bytes)
| filter src_if = "inside" and dst_if = "outside" and src_host != null and dst_host != null
| alter int_host = src_host, ext_host = dst_host
| bin _time span = 1h
| comp count() as outbound_conns,
       values(dst_port) as ext_ports,
       values(src_port) as int_ports,
       values(proto) as protocols
       by int_host, ext_host, _time
| join type = inner (
    dataset = infoblox_infoblox_raw
    | filter _raw_log contains "NOERROR" and (_raw_log contains "c2-infra" or _raw_log contains "command-control" or _raw_log contains "phishing" or _raw_log contains "new-c2")
    | alter int_src = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "client (?:@0x\w+ )?(\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)#"), 0),
            bad_domain = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "query: (\S+) IN"), 0)
    | filter int_src != null
    | comp count() as dns_count, values(bad_domain) as bad_domains by int_src
    | fields int_src, dns_count, bad_domains
  ) as dns int_host = dns.int_src
| fields int_host, ext_host, ext_ports, int_ports, protocols, bad_domains, outbound_conns
description: Cisco ASA Built 302013 outbound connection from an internal host that also resolved a c2-infra/command-control domain (NOERROR) — bypassed both DNS RPZ and threat-block layers.
alert_name: Cisco ASA — Outbound C2 Connection Allowed (Post DNS Resolve)
alert_description:
What fired: Cisco ASA Built 302013 outbound connection from an internal host that also resolved a c2-infra/command-control domain (NOERROR) — bypassed both DNS RPZ and threat-block layers.

Why it matters: a host is communicating with known-bad or anomalous infrastructure (C2 / malicious domain). Assessed severity: High.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1071 - Application Layer Protocol (TA0011 - Command and Control).

Investigate:
  - Identify the internal client and the domain/IP contacted, and check reputation + resolution history.
  - Look for the initial delivery vector (email/web/download) and any beaconing cadence or follow-on payloads from the same host.
  - Pivot on the alert's key entity (int_host) to related activity in the same window.
  - Confirm the activity is not expected/authorized for the involved entity before escalating.
